rule: Hypertrophy/accessory sets are halved on days 2-3 after any Red day, whatever today's readiness (v1)
summary: No study tests a blanket 72 h accessory-volume cut after a low-readiness day. The HRV-guided trials this system follows adjust the day the signal is low and train normally once it recovers, which is the same reasoning behind the 2026-11-22 change of the Red carry to 'next day follows its own readiness'. Recovery studies in trained men show neuromuscular fatigue from non-failure sets clearing within 24-48 h (high-volume/failure work up to 48 h), so a fixed 72 h window has no specific basis. Cost per firing is small (1-2 sessions of accessory volume) but it fires after every Red, including non-training Reds such as a bad night. Proposed: Code PR (bump to v2): halve accessory sets on days 2-3 after a Red only when that Red was joint-driven (same condition as the v2 Red carry) or today's readiness is Yellow/Red; on a Green day after a non-joint Red, train as planned. Wrong if, over the next block, sessions within 3 days of a non-joint Red show higher session RPE at the same loads or a second Red follows within 72 h more often than before.

sources.note: HRV-guided runners: hard session if HRV in SWC band, otherwise easy that day; no multi-day carry-over cut, and performance improved
Daily HRV decisions (low day -> easy/rest that day; high again -> hard) beat predefined training; adjustments were day-by-day
Squat fatigue (velocity vs 1 m/s load, CMJ) recovered by 24-48 h; higher velocity loss slowed recovery
Sets to failure kept CMJ down up to 48 h; half-the-possible reps recovered faster - fatigue window depends on proximity to failure, not a fixed 72 h
Delphi: reduced-load periods are a fatigue-management tool, but the consensus says nothing about a 72 h per-Red volume cut
